title: Chapter 10. Nayanananda and Balarama Dasa: the Gaura-avatara, the Kirtanas of Navadvipa, Gaura and Gadadhara, Shantipura
html:
Padas of Nayanananda (Nayana Mishra), the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara Pandita, and padas signed by Balarama Dasa, in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara; the kirtanas of Navadvipa, where Gaura dances beside Gadadhara; Gauranga's form; His bhava — the Lord weeps gazing at Gadadhara's face; a spring night on the Ganga and the spring swing; Shantipura after the sannyasa and the departure for Nilachala; Nityananda in Gauda. Majumdar counts Nayanananda among the Lord's contemporaries: like his other padas, the pada on Gaura and Gadadhara ("premera gṛhiṇī se paṇḍita gadādhare") is cited by Narahari Chakravarti in the Bhakti-ratnakara as testimony; for Balarama Dasa Majumdar accepts three padas from the Bhakti-ratnakara (many padas of a later Balarama Dasa bear the same signature, so the attribution of the rest is doubtful). The text follows the Padakalpataru (PK), checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus, the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Balarama Dasa — "kaliyuga-matta-mataṅgaja-maradane…" (PK 617)

Praise of the Gaura-avatara: the age of Kali is a mad elephant, Gaura is the king of lions who has appeared in the mountain cave of Navadvipa; at the roar of sankirtana sins and the mystic perfections flee, and on the wretched He hangs necklaces of the pearls of the holy name. The gaura-chandrika at the opening of PK's 3rd shakha. Raga kamoda.1

কলিযুগ-মত্ত-মতঙ্গজ-মরদনে
কুমতি-করিণি দুর গেল ।
পামর দুরগত নাম-মোতি শত-
দাম কণ্ঠ ভরি দেল ॥

kaliyuga-matta-mataṅgaja-maradane
kumati-kariṇi dura gela |
pāmara duragata nāma-moti śata-
dāma kaṇṭha bhari dela ||

kaliyuga — of the Kali age; matta-mataṅgaja — of the mad elephant; maradane — at the crushing; kumati-kariṇi — the she-elephant of evil thinking; dura gela — went far away; pāmara — to the low; duragata — to the wretched; nāma-moti — pearls of the Name; śata-dāma — a hundred-stranded necklace; kaṇṭha bhari — filling the neck; dela — gave (put on)

1.1When the mad elephant of the Kali age was crushed,
the she-elephant of evil thinking fled far away;
on the low and the wretched He hung, as much as their necks would hold,
hundred-stranded necklaces of the pearls of the Name.2

অপরূপ গৌর বিরাজ ।
শ্রীনবদ্বীপ-নগর-গিরি-কন্দরে
উয়ল কেশরি-রাজ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

aparūpa gaura birāja |
śrīnabadvīpa-nagara-giri-kandare
uyala keśari-rāja || dhru ||

aparūpa — wondrously; gaura — Gaura; birāja — shines; śrī-nabadvīpa-nagara — of the city of Sri Navadvipa; giri-kandare — in the mountain cave; uyala — has risen; keśari-rāja — the king of lions

1.2(Refrain) Wondrously shines Gaura:
in the mountain cave of the city of Sri Navadvipa
the king of lions has risen!

সংকীর্ত্তন-রণ হুঙ্কৃতি শুনইতে
দুরিত দীপি-গণ ভাগি ।
ভয়ে আকুল অণিমাদি মৃগীকুল
পুণবত গরব তেয়াগি ॥

saṃkīrttana-raṇa huṅkṛti śunaite
durita dīpi-gaṇa bhāgi |
bhaye ākula aṇimādi mṛgīkula
puṇabata garaba teyāgi ||

saṅkīrttana-raṇa — the battle (cry) of sankirtana; huṅkṛti — the roar; śunaite — on hearing; durita — the sins; dīpi-gaṇa — the leopards; bhāgi — flee; bhaye ākula — frantic with fear; aṇimādi — anima and the rest (the perfections); mṛgīkula — the herd of does; puṇabata — (merits?, the word is unclear); garaba — the pride; teyāgi — abandoning

1.3Hearing the battle roar of sankirtana,
the leopards — the sins — run away;
the does — anima and the other perfections — are frantic with fear,
abandoning the pride of their merits.3

ত্যাগ যাগ যম তিরিথি বরত সম
শশ জম্বুকি জরি যাতি ।
বলরাম দাস কহ অতয়ে সে জগ মাহ
হরি-ধনি শবদ খেয়াতি ॥

tyāga yāga yama tirithi barata sama
śaśa jambuki jari yāti |
balarāma dāsa kaha ataye se jaga māha
hari-dhani śabada kheyāti ||

tyāga — renunciation; yāga — sacrifices; yama — the vows of yama; tirithi — pilgrimages; barata — fasts (vows); sama — like; śaśa — hares; jambuki — jackals; jari — scorched; yāti — flee; balarāma dāsa kaha — Balarama Dasa says; ataye — therefore; se — that; jaga māha — in the world; hari-dhani śabada — the sound of Hari's name; kheyāti — is renowned

1.4Renunciation, sacrifices, the vows of yama, pilgrimages, fasts —
like hares and jackals they flee as if scorched.
Balarama Dasa says: that is why in the world
only the sound of Hari's name is renowned.4

(gaura-chandrika), no. 1 (label "॥১॥৬১৭॥"); raga kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 1091. GPT1 — p. 25, no. 1 (kamoda). The catalogue's link to the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR p. 901) is mistaken: there it is a different pada signed by Narahari — "bali-kali-matta-mataṅgaja-maradana gaurasiṃha nācata nadīyāya". The pada is in elaborate Vrajabuli; which of the Balarama Dasas wrote it is not established. "ca": "far" (dūra). MS "ka": "pearl" (motima); so also GPT1. "Hundred-stranded necklaces" — śata-dāma, a necklace of many strands. sankirtana they lose their worth, like does before a lion. The word "puṇabata" (here "merits," from puṇya) is unclear; MS "ka" has "pumabata," "kha," "gha," "ca" "pumarata," P-R-Sa "patharata." MSS "ka," "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "islands" (dvīpagaṇa) instead of "leopards" (dīpigaṇa); MSS "ka," "gha," "ca": "forest" (bana), "kha": "in the forest" instead of "battle" (raṇa). thought: nama-sankirtana is the dharma of the age of Kali (cf. CC Adi 3, 17), and all other means give way before it.

2. Balarama Dasa — "baṛa abatāra bhāi baṛa abatāra…" (PK 2207 = BR p. 956)

The great incarnation: Gaura distributes the storehouse of prema to the fallen; women of noble families dance in the sankirtana; the one whom all drove away as untouchable is now the one whose foot-dust the gods beg for; even yavanas sing the holy name. Raga shri (BR — dhanashi).5

বড় অবতার ভাই বড় অবতার ।
পতিতেরে বিলাওল প্রেমের ভাণ্ডার ॥

baṛa abatāra bhāi baṛa abatāra |
patitere bilāola premera bhāṇḍāra ||

baṛa abatāra — a great incarnation; bhāi — brothers; patitere — to the fallen; bilāola — gave away; premera bhāṇḍāra — the storehouse of prema

2.1A great incarnation, brothers, a great incarnation!
To the fallen He has given away the storehouse of prema.

বড় অপরূপ গোরাচাঁদের লীলা ।
রাজা হৈয়া কান্ধে করে বৈষ্ণবের দোলা ॥

baṛa aparūpa gorācām̐dera līlā |
rājā haiyā kāndhe kare baiṣṇabera dolā ||

baṛa aparūpa — how wondrous; gorācām̐dera līlā — Gorachand's pastimes; rājā haiyā — being a king; kāndhe kare — holds on the shoulder; baiṣṇabera dolā — a Vaishnava's palanquin

2.2How wondrous are Gorachand's pastimes:
a king — and he carries a Vaishnava's palanquin on his shoulder!6

হেন অবতারের উপমা দিতে নারি ।
সংকীর্ত্তন মাঝে নাচে কুলের বৌহারী ॥

hena abatārera upamā dite nāri |
saṃkīrttana mājhe nāce kulera bauhārī ||

hena abatārera — for such an incarnation; upamā dite nāri — I cannot give a likeness; saṅkīrttana mājhe — amid the sankirtana; nāce — dance; kulera bauhārī — the wives (and daughters) of noble families

2.3No likeness can be found for such an incarnation:
amid the sankirtana the wives of noble families dance.7

সর্ব্ব লোক ছাড়ে যারে অপরশ বলি ।
দেবগণ মাগে এবে তার পদধূলি ॥

sarvva loka chāṛe yāre aparaśa bali |
debagaṇa māge ebe tāra padadhūli ||

sarva loka — all people; chāṛe — shun; yāre — whom; aparaśa bali — calling him "untouchable"; debagaṇa — the gods; māge — beg; ebe — now; tāra padadhūli — the dust of his feet

2.4The one whom everyone shunned, saying, "Do not touch!" —
from him the gods now beg the dust of his feet.

যবনেহ নাচে গায় লয় হরিনাম ।
হেন অবতারে সে বঞ্চিত বলরাম ॥

yabaneha nāce gāya laya harināma |
hena abatāre se bañcita balarāma ||

yabaneha — even the yavanas; nāce gāya — dance, sing; laya harināma — take Hari's name; hena abatāre — in such an incarnation; se — he; bañcita — deprived; balarāma — Balarama

2.5Even yavanas dance, sing and take the name of Hari —
yet in such an incarnation Balarama is left out.8

prakārāntara," no. 24 (label "॥২৪॥২২০৭॥"); raga shri; P-R-Sa MS no. 2315, P-R 9.15. BR, 12th wave (1913 ed., pp. 956–957, "punardhānaśī"): the pada is sung within the account of Navadvipa. Majumdar cites it among the BR testimonies of Balarama Dasa (the detail of the noble wives dancing in the sankirtana is new). The catalogue had assigned it to PK 2208, which is a pada of Ananta Dasa. GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 36. (Prataparudra) humbly serving the Vaishnavas. BR: "a Vaishnava's bag (jholā)" instead of "palanquin (dolā)"; MS P-R: "bears" (bahe) instead of "holds." (CB Madhya 23; CC Adi 17).

3. Nayanananda — "jaya re jaya re gorā śrīśacī-nandana…" (PK 2)

Glory to Gora, the son of Shachi, dancing His auspicious dance: Srivasa, Ramananda, Mukunda and Vasu sing; the mridanga and the mandiras resound; one anoints Gora with sandal paste, another puts on Him a malati garland; some call Him Rama, others the Kandarpa dear to Radha, but the poet knows only this: He is Gadadhara's life. A mangalacharana — the second pada of PK. Raga kamoda.9

জয় রে জয় রে গোরা শ্রীশচী-নন্দন
মঙ্গল নটন সুঠান রে ।
কীর্ত্তন-আনন্দে শ্রীবাস রামানন্দে
মুকুন্দ বাসু গুণ-গান রে ॥

jaya re jaya re gorā śrīśacī-nandana
maṅgala naṭana suṭhāna re |
kīrttana-ānande śrībāsa rāmānande
mukunda bāsu guṇa-gāna re ||

jaya re jaya re — glory, glory; gorā — to Gora; śrī-śacī-nandana — the son of Sri Shachi; maṅgala naṭana — in the auspicious dance; suṭhāna — beautiful; re — (refrain particle); kīrttana-ānande — in the bliss of kirtana; śrībāsa rāmānande — Srivasa and Ramananda; mukunda bāsu — Mukunda and Vasu; guṇa-gāna — sing His virtues

3.1Glory, glory to Gora, the son of Sri Shachi,
beautiful in His auspicious dance!
In the bliss of kirtana Srivasa and Ramananda,
Mukunda and Vasu sing His virtues.10

দাং দ্রিমিকি দ্রিমি মাদল বাজত
মধুর মঞ্জীর রসাল রে ।
শঙ্খ করতাল ঘণ্টারব ভেল
মিলল পদতলে তাল রে ॥

dāṃ drimiki drimi mādala bājata
madhura mañjīra rasāla re |
śaṅkha karatāla ghaṇṭāraba bhela
milala padatale tāla re ||

dāṃ drimiki drimi — (the sound of the madal); mādala bājata — the madal sounds; madhura — sweetly; mañjīra — the mandiras (small cymbals); rasāla — ring delightfully; śaṅkha — conch; karatāla — karatalas; ghaṇṭāraba — the ringing of bells; bhela — arises; milala — blended; padatale tāla — with the rhythm of the feet

3.2"Dang drimiki drimi" — the madal sounds,
the mandiras ring sweetly,
conch, karatalas and bells resound,
blending with the rhythm of His feet.11

কো দেই গোরা-অঙ্গে সুগন্ধি চন্দন
কো দেই মালতী-মাল রে ।
পিরিতি-ফুল-শরে মরম ভেদল
ভাবে সহচর ভোর রে ॥

ko dei gorā-aṅge sugandhi candana
ko dei mālatī-māla re |
piriti-phula-śare marama bhedala
bhābe sahacara bhora re ||

ko dei — one applies; gorā-aṅge — to Gora's body; sugandhi candana — fragrant sandal paste; ko dei — one puts on; mālatī-māla — a malati garland; piriti-phula-śare — by the flower-arrow of love; marama bhedala — the heart is pierced; bhābe — in bhava; sahacara — the companions; bhora — are lost

3.3One anoints Gora's body with fragrant sandal paste,
another puts on Him a malati garland;
pierced to the heart by the flower-arrow of love,
the companions are lost in bhava.12

কোই বোলে গোরা জানকী-বল্লভ
রাধার প্রিয় পাঁচবাণ রে ।
নয়নানন্দ মনে আন নাহি জানে
আমারি গদাধরের প্রাণ রে ॥

koi bole gorā jānakī-ballabha
rādhāra priya pām̐cabāṇa re |
nayanānanda mane āna nāhi jāne
āmāri gadādharera prāṇa re ||

koi bole — some say; gorā — Gora; jānakī-ballabha — the beloved of Janaki (Rama); rādhāra priya — dear to Radha; pām̐cabāṇa — the Five-arrowed One (Kandarpa); nayanānanda mane — in Nayanananda's heart (mind); āna nāhi jāne — knows nothing else; āmāri gadādharera prāṇa — the life of my Gadadhara

3.4Some say Gora is the beloved of Janaki,
others — the Five-arrowed One dear to Radha;
Nayanananda's heart knows nothing else:
He is the life of my Gadadhara.13

"॥২॥"); raga kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 1, P-R 1.3 and 38.1 (raga "kamoda-mallara," P-R "mallara"). KGC — 30th kshanada (purnima), no. 1, gaura-chandrika (kedara); GPT1 — p. 4, no. 4 (kedara or mangala); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 4. The catalogue gave the PK number as "45" (PK 45 is a pada of Radhamohana on Radha's purvaraga). house where the night kirtanas of Navadvipa were held; Ramananda here is probably Vasu Ramananda; Mukunda is the singer Mukunda Datta; Vasu is Vasudeva (Vasu) Ghosha. drimi"; P-R 1.3: "drimiki drimiki drimi"; P-R 38.1: "dāṃ drimi drimi," "mandirā"; KGC: "drāṃ drimiki drimi." Mandiras are small cymbals. 38.1: "One anoints Gora's body with sandal paste, (one offers) fragrant karabira," "kora re" instead of "bhora re." MSS "kha," "gha," "ca," P-R, P-R-Sa: "the (female) companions" (sahacari). The flower-arrow is Kamadeva's weapon; here it is the hearts pierced by love for the Lord. Five-arrowed One is Kamadeva; "the Five-arrowed One dear to Radha" is Krishna as the transcendental Madana (aprakrita-madana, CC Madhya 8), not the worldly god of desire. Gadadhara Pandita, according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, is a manifestation of Radha; Nayanananda calls Gaura the life of his Gadadhara. MSS "ka," P-R-Sa: "āmāra"; P-R: "hāmāri."

4. Balarama Dasa — "bhāla raṅge nāce mora śacīra dulāla…" (BR p. 837)

Gaura dances in the kirtana of Navadvipa: sandal paste all over His body, His garland swaying, pearls on His chest, His ankle bells ringing; the kinnaras learn singing from Him, the gandharvas contemplate His dance; the lotuses shrink before His eyes. Raga dhanashi.14

ভাল রঙ্গে নাচে মোর শচীর দুলাল ।
সব অঙ্গে চন্দন দোলয়ে বনমাল ॥

bhāla raṅge nāce mora śacīra dulāla |
saba aṅge candana dolaye banamāla ||

bhāla raṅge — beautifully, joyfully; nāce — dances; mora — my; śacīra dulāla — Shachi's darling; saba aṅge — on all the body; candana — sandal paste; dolaye — sways; banamāla — the garland

4.1How beautifully my darling of Shachi dances!
Sandal paste over all His body, His garland swaying.

বিশাল হৃদয়ে গজমুকুতার হার ।
পদতলে তাল উঠে নূপুর-ঝঙ্কার ॥

biśāla hṛdaye gajamukutāra hāra |
padatale tāla uṭhe nūpura-jhaṅkāra ||

biśāla hṛdaye — on the broad chest; gaja-mukutāra hāra — a necklace of "elephant" pearls; padatale — beneath the feet; tāla uṭhe — the rhythm rises; nūpura-jhaṅkāra — the ringing of the ankle bells

4.2On His broad chest is a necklace of "elephant" pearls,
to the rhythm of His feet the ankle bells ring out.15

ছন্দ-বিছন্দে কত জানে অঙ্গভঙ্গি ।
নদীয়া-নগরে নাই এত বড় রঙ্গী ॥

chanda-bichande kata jāne aṅgabhaṅgi |
nadīyā-nagare nāi eta baṛa raṅgī ||

chanda-bichande — in measure and out of measure; kata — how many; jāne — He knows; aṅga-bhaṅgi — bends of the body; nadīyā-nagare — in the city of Nadia; nāi — there is not; eta baṛa raṅgī — so great an artist (merrymaker)

4.3How many bends of the body He knows, in measure and out of measure —
in all the city of Nadia there is no such artist!16

কিন্নর করয়ে শিক্ষা শুনি মৃদু গান ।
গন্ধর্ব্ব তাণ্ডব হেরি ধরয়ে ধিয়ান ॥

kinnara karaye śikṣā śuni mṛdu gāna |
gandharvva tāṇḍaba heri dharaye dhiyāna ||

kinnara — the kinnaras; karaye śikṣā — learn; śuni — hearing; mṛdu gāna — the soft singing; gandharva — the gandharvas; tāṇḍaba heri — seeing the tandava; dharaye dhiyāna — sink into meditation

4.4The kinnaras learn from hearing His soft singing,
the gandharvas, seeing His tandava, sink into meditation.17

পঙ্কজ সঙ্কোচ পায় দেখিয়া নয়নে ।
হাসিতে বিজুরি-ছটা পড়য়ে দশনে ॥

paṅkaja saṅkoca pāya dekhiyā nayane |
hāsite bijuri-chaṭā paṛaye daśane ||

paṅkaja — the lotus; saṅkoca pāya — shrinks; dekhiyā nayane — seeing (His) eyes; hāsite — when He smiles; bijuri-chaṭā — the radiance of lightning; paṛaye daśane — falls from His teeth

4.5The lotus shrinks on seeing His eyes,
when He smiles, His teeth shed the radiance of lightning.

বান্ধুলি জিনিয়া রাঙা ওটখানি হাস ।
ও-রূপ হেরিয়া কান্দে বলরাম দাস ॥

bāndhuli jiniyā rāṅā oṭakhāni hāsa |
o-rūpa heriyā kānde balarāma dāsa ||

bāndhuli jiniyā — surpassing the bandhuli flower; rāṅā — red; oṭakhāni — the lips; hāsa — the smile; o-rūpa heriyā — gazing at that form; kānde — weeps; balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa

4.6His lips are redder than the bandhuli flower — and that smile!
Gazing at this form, Balarama Dasa weeps.18

1884–1889. The pada is not in PK or GPT1. In Narahari Chakravarti it is sung in the account of the path by which the Lord went with kirtana from Srivasa's house to the Ganga and back; Majumdar cites it among the three BR padas of Balarama Dasa. (ringing). "oṭakhāni hāsa."

5. Balarama Dasa — "hari hari maṅgala bharala khiti-maṇḍala…" (PK 2065)

Gaura dances, spreading through the world the storehouse of rasa — the kirtana of His own virtues; His form robs Manmatha of his senses; the Name that Shiva and Brahma seek in the depths of the heart He strings into a necklace and gives to the fallen. Raga mangala.19

হরি হরি মঙ্গল ভরল খিতি-মণ্ডল
রসময় রতন-পসার ।
